title: CI-failure remediation on factory-owned branches, behind the flake gate and strike budget
description:
The loop with teeth: CI fails on a branch the factory owns, the factory dispatches a run to fix it.

TWO GOVERNORS, both named in the epic scope and both load-bearing:
- THE FLAKE GATE. A test that fails intermittently must not spend money being 'fixed' repeatedly. Establish that a failure is reproducible before dispatching. This repo has already been burned by load-dependent flakes (vy2, and a TestSmokeGolden flake during Phase 2 that a bisect settled), so the gate is not theoretical.
- THE STRIKE BUDGET. A run that fails to fix a failure gets a bounded number of attempts, then escalates to a human instead of looping. Phase 2's cost lesson applies: an agent that does not converge costs 100% of its tokens for 0% of the work.

FACTORY-OWNED BRANCHES ONLY. This must never push to a branch a human owns, and 'owns' has to be structural — a branch-name convention plus the credential grade, not a check the prompt is asked to respect.

acceptance_criteria: A reproducible CI failure on a factory-owned branch gets a fix attempt; a flaky failure does not; a run that strikes out escalates rather than retrying; nothing can dispatch against a human-owned branch.
closed_reason: Completed: CI-failure remediation on factory-owned branches, behind both governors. Branch ownership is enforced by the TYPE SYSTEM rather than a check — factoryOwnedBranch() is the only constructor of a branded FactoryOwnedBranch, CheckFailureFacts.branch is that type, and dispatchRemediation accepts only those facts, so a human-owned branch cannot be expressed as a dispatchable input rather than merely being rejected by one. The flake gate establishes reproducibility before spending, and a run that strikes out escalates to a human instead of looping.
